nt: The phrase **you have gone astray** follows a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended. The standard written Hebrew text as we have it today spells this word in a way that is difficult to understand here. The correction fits the context better, since Jeremiah is speaking to the people about what they themselves have done. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [you have led yourselves astray]

Jeremiah is using **you have gone astray at your lives** as a common expression of the culture. Here it could mean: (1) “you have gone astray at the cost of your lives.” Alternate translation: [you have made a mistake that will cost you your lives] (2) that the Judeans had gone astray in their “souls” or “inner selves” because the Hebrew word translated as “at your lives” could be translated “in your souls.” Alternate translation: [you deceived yourselves] or [you were insincere]

Jeremiah is stating the pronoun **you** separately, even though the verb translated as **you sent** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that it was the people themselves who had asked him to go to Yahweh for them. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [it was you who sent me]
